minutes.headline: Committee narrows town building priorities to Town Hall/Ritter and Turkey Hill; TC Pacios left undecided
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee approved three sets of prior minutes and reviewed feedback from other town committees on its draft master plan recommendations. Most of the meeting focused on prioritizing major town building projects for the next decade, converging on Town Hall/Ritter and Turkey Hill as the top near-term priorities, with Marshall Park and TC Pacios as the next tier, while leaving the Brooks House slated for sale or lease rather than town investment.

what_happened.line: The committee narrowed its near-term building priority list to Town Hall/Ritter and Turkey Hill, with Marshall Park and TC Pacios ranked just behind.
Brooks House and 925 Mass Avenue stay on the list as candidates for sale or lease, not for town capital construction spending.
Athletic field improvements at the middle/high school are already moving forward as a separate item for the May annual town meeting, outside this list.
A roof repair project for TC Pacios may go before voters at a special town meeting, though no long-term use for the building has been settled.
The committee approved minutes from three prior meetings, with corrections, and reviewed feedback from other town committees on its draft plan.

why_it_matters: This priority list is an early step toward what capital projects the town could eventually ask taxpayers to fund, so where a building lands on it -- or off it, like Brooks House -- signals what kind of ballot question residents may see later.
A TC Pacios roof question at a special town meeting would be a near-term vote, separate from this longer-range prioritization.

The threshold discussed for what makes this list -- roughly projects beyond the capital planning committee's typical annual budget -- shapes which future building repairs residents vote on directly versus which are handled through routine capital planning.
